titleZh: 海外客人到店，你准备好了吗？
titleEn: Overseas Guests Are Arriving. Is Your Hotel Ready?
summaryZh: 接待海外客人不只是会说英语。酒店需要逐项验证入住沟通、支付说明、设施信息、应急支持和跨班次跟进是否真正连续。
summaryEn: Serving overseas guests requires more than English. Hotels should verify check-in communication, payment explanations, facility information, emergency support and cross-shift follow-up.
contentZh:
海外客人到店，你准备好了吗？

想象一个常见场景：一家酒店接待了几位海外客人，入住过程基本完成，但客人在第二天早上反复来到前台，问的问题都很简单——早餐几点结束、健身房在哪里、昨晚报修的空调怎么处理了。

前台觉得自己已经说清楚了。客人觉得什么都没得到回答。

这不是语言能力的问题，而是服务连续性的问题。入境客服务不是把中文翻译成英文，而是确保客人在每一个关键时刻能表达需求、完成必要操作、找到负责人并得到后续回应。

很多酒店认为自己"可以接待外宾"，因为前台有人会说几句英语，大堂有英文标识。但客人到店后真正需要的，不是一句"Welcome"，而是在五个具体环节上不被卡住。

可以用五个服务断点做一次体检，看看你的酒店到底准备好了没有。

断点一：到店交流能否完成基本信息传递

客人到店的第一件事是完成入住。这个过程需要传递的信息远比"护照、信用卡、签名"复杂。

WiFi密码怎么连接、电梯在哪个方向、房间钥匙卡如何使用、早上几点可以退房、遇到问题打哪个电话——这些信息如果用中文说一遍，客人可能点头表示理解。但如果客人实际上没有听懂，他会在接下来的几个小时里反复回到前台。

检查方法很简单：找一个不会说中文的朋友，模拟一次入住说明。观察他在哪个环节开始困惑、在哪里点头但其实没有理解。

断点二：支付与押金说明是否清楚到不需要重复询问

海外客人在支付环节遇到的障碍，往往不是"不能刷卡"，而是"不知道会发生什么"。

预授权会冻结多少金额、什么时候解冻、押金用什么方式退还、如果提前退房费用怎么计算——这些问题如果在前台没有主动说明，客人会在入住期间反复确认，甚至在退房时产生争议。

很多酒店对国内客人的押金说明已经形成习惯，但对海外客人往往只停留在"能刷卡就行"的层面。实际上，支付说明的清晰度直接决定退房时的满意度和评价。

检查方法：让前台在模拟入住时，用英文或简单英文加手势，把预授权金额、解冻时间和退还方式说一遍。如果前台自己都觉得说不清楚，客人一定更不清楚。

断点三：设施与服务时间的信息是否可独立获取

客人入住后需要使用的设施——早餐时间、健身房位置、洗衣服务、客房送物——这些信息在中文环境下已经通过标识、口头说明和手机扫码解决了。但对海外客人，这些信息是否同样可获取？

一家酒店可能在大堂挂了英文标识，但餐厅门口只有中文菜单、健身房的使用说明只有中文、洗衣袋上的说明客人看不懂。这些零散的信息缺失，会让客人在每一次使用设施时都需要找人帮忙。

检查方法：从客人走出电梯开始，走一遍去餐厅、健身房、洗衣房和商务中心的路线。在每一个节点检查：如果客人不懂中文，他能否独立完成他想做的事？

断点四：紧急及在地信息是否有人主动提供

客人在陌生城市遇到紧急情况——生病、物品丢失、需要打车去机场——他首先会找前台。

如果前台只能回答"我可以帮你叫车"，但无法提供附近医院信息、无法协助报警沟通、无法说明退房后的行李寄存和交通方案，客人的安全感会迅速下降。

这不是要求前台成为旅行顾问，而是要求酒店准备一份基本的英文应急信息卡：附近医院地址和电话、报警和急救电话、最近的地铁站和出租车招呼点、退房后的行李寄存政策。

检查方法：问前台三个问题——"如果客人半夜生病怎么办？""如果客人丢了护照怎么办？""如果客人需要凌晨去机场怎么办？"如果三个问题都需要现查或现问，说明这个断点还没有被处理。

断点五：跨班次的问题跟进是否有人负责

客人晚上反映了一个问题，第二天早上发现没有人处理。这是一个在入境客服务中容易出现的高风险场景。

国内客人可能会再次找到前台或者打电话催促。海外客人可能不会——他会直接离开，然后在预订平台上写一条差评。

跨班次跟进不是靠个人责任心，而是靠交接机制。如果酒店的班次交接只记录房态和特殊要求，不记录"客人反映的问题和处理进度"，那么跨班次断档就是必然的。

检查方法：抽查最近一周的班次交接记录，看是否有客人需求的跟进记录。如果没有，说明这个机制还不存在。

验收方法：客人能否完成，而不是酒店是否配置

五个断点的检查逻辑是一致的：不是问"酒店有没有英文标识""有没有英文菜单""有没有应急方案"，而是问"客人能否独立完成他需要做的事"。

标识存在不等于客人看懂了。菜单有英文不等于客人知道在哪里。方案存在不等于有人执行。

验收标准只有一个：客人能否在每一个关键节点完成他需要完成的事。

复查指标

完成五个断点的修复后，可以用以下指标验证改善效果：

前台被同一客人重复询问同一问题的频率是否下降。海外客人的支付相关争议是否减少。涉及沟通和服务连续性的评价关键词是否改善。夜间报修和需求的次日完成率是否提升。

这些指标比"我们增加了英文标识"更能说明问题。

如果你的酒店正在检查入境客服务的服务连续性，可以从一次酒店运营管理诊断开始，把五个断点的现状和修复优先级理清楚。也可以直接预约酒店经营诊断，用一次前台至夜班的全流程演练验证真实承接能力。

参考来源：
- 国务院办公厅《关于进一步优化支付服务提升支付便利性的意见》（2024年）：https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/202403/content_6937623.htm
contentEn:
Overseas Guests Are Arriving. Is Your Hotel Ready?

Consider a common scenario: a hotel hosts several overseas guests. Check-in goes smoothly. But the next morning, guests keep returning to the front desk with simple questions—when does breakfast end, where is the gym, what happened to the maintenance request from last night?

The front desk believed they had communicated clearly. The guests felt they had received no answers.

This is not a language problem. It is a service continuity problem. Serving overseas guests is not about translating Chinese into English. It is about ensuring that guests can express needs, complete necessary tasks, find the right person, and receive follow-up at every critical moment.

Many hotels believe they "can receive foreign guests" because someone at the front desk speaks some English and the lobby has English signage. But what guests actually need after arrival is not a "Welcome"—it is not getting stuck at five specific service points.

Use these five service gaps to check whether your hotel is truly ready.

Gap One: Can Check-In Communication Deliver All Necessary Information?

The first thing a guest needs at check-in goes well beyond passport, credit card, and signature.

WiFi connection details, elevator direction, how the key card works, checkout time, who to call for problems—these need to be communicated clearly. If the information is delivered only in Chinese, the guest may nod in agreement but actually understand nothing. The result is repeated trips to the front desk over the next few hours.

A simple test: ask someone who does not speak Chinese to simulate a check-in. Observe where they start to look confused, where they nod but clearly have not understood.

Gap Two: Are Payment and Deposit Explanations Clear Enough to Prevent Repeated Questions?

The payment obstacle for overseas guests is usually not "the card doesn't work." It is "I don't know what will happen."

How much will be pre-authorized? When will it be released? How is the deposit refunded? What happens to charges if I check out early? If these are not proactively explained, guests will ask repeatedly during their stay—and often dispute them at checkout.

Many hotels have developed habits for explaining deposits to domestic guests, but for overseas guests, the standard stops at "the card works." In reality, payment explanation clarity directly determines checkout satisfaction and review scores.

Test: ask your front desk to explain the pre-authorization amount, release timeline, and refund method in simple English. If they struggle, the guest will struggle more.

Gap Three: Can Guests Independently Access Facility and Service Information?

After check-in, guests need to use facilities—breakfast hours, gym location, laundry service, room delivery. For Chinese-speaking guests, this information is available through signage, verbal instructions, and QR codes. For overseas guests, is it equally accessible?

A hotel may have English signs in the lobby, but the restaurant has only a Chinese menu, gym instructions are in Chinese only, and laundry bags have no English guidance. Each small gap forces the guest to find someone for help.

Test: walk from the elevator to the restaurant, gym, laundry, and business center. At each point, ask: if the guest does not read Chinese, can they independently do what they need to do?

Gap Four: Are Emergency and Local Information Proactively Provided?

When guests face an emergency in an unfamiliar city—illness, lost items, need to reach the airport—they go to the front desk first.

If the front desk can only say "I can call a taxi for you" but cannot provide nearby hospital information, assist with police communication, or explain luggage storage and transport options after checkout, the guest's sense of security drops quickly.

This does not require the front desk to become travel consultants. It requires a basic English emergency information card: nearby hospital address and phone number, emergency numbers, nearest metro station and taxi point, post-checkout luggage policy.

Test: ask the front desk three questions—"What if a guest gets sick at midnight?" "What if a guest loses their passport?" "What if a guest needs to reach the airport at dawn?" If all three require looking things up or asking someone, this gap has not been addressed.

Gap Five: Is Cross-Shift Follow-Up Owned by Someone?

A guest reports a problem at night. By morning, no one has followed up. This is a high-risk scenario that can quickly affect overseas guest satisfaction.

A domestic guest might return to the desk or call to follow up. An overseas guest often will not—they will simply leave and write a negative review on the booking platform.

Cross-shift follow-up depends not on individual diligence but on handover mechanisms. If shift handover records only track room status and special requests, not "guest issues and resolution progress," then cross-shift breakdowns are inevitable.

Test: review the past week's shift handover records. Are there follow-up entries for guest requests? If not, the mechanism does not yet exist.

Verification: Can the Guest Complete Each Task?

The checking logic for all five gaps is the same. Do not ask "Does the hotel have English signage?" or "Is there an English menu?" or "Is there an emergency plan?" Ask instead: "Can the guest independently complete what they need to do?"

Signage existing does not mean the guest understood it. A menu in English does not mean the guest knows where to find it. A plan existing does not mean someone executes it.

The only acceptance criterion: can the guest complete every critical task at every key point?

Review Indicators

After addressing the five gaps, verify improvement using these indicators:

Has the frequency of the same guest asking the same question repeatedly decreased? Have payment-related disputes from overseas guests declined? Have review keywords related to communication and service continuity improved? Has the next-day completion rate for nighttime maintenance requests increased?

These indicators tell you more than "we added English signs."

If your hotel is checking service continuity for overseas guests, consider starting with a hotel operations advisory review to clarify the current state and repair priorities across the five gaps. You can also request an operations diagnosis to validate real readiness through a full front-desk-to-night-shift drill.

References:
- State Council opinion on payment convenience (2024): https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/202403/content_6937623.htm
author: 迈创兄弟C&T
